# beowulf-fitt-32 — drafter's cruces and guesses

No dotted vowel occurs in lines 2221-2311, so no metrical-dot sentence is needed.

## Damaged or corrupt text
- 2226b `† mwatide`: untranslated; Thorpe/Schücking/Chambers inwlātode, Holthausen hē wagode, Sedgefield þæt geīode listed in the note.
- 2227-2230: lost stretches; only gyst(e) / gryrebrōga, (earm)sceapen, sceapen, (þā hyne) se fǣr begeat survive. Referent of hyne (2230) taken to be the thief by inference only.
- 2231 lost verb (Grein sōhte; Heyne/Trautmann/Chambers geseah; Holthausen genōm).
- 2223 þ(ēow) vs þ(egn); 2225 (ærnes) þearfa; 2221 wyrmhord ābræc (MS horda/cræft) and 2225 fealh (MS weal/weall).
- 2239 weard (noun "guardian") vs wearð (Thorpe, Holthausen, Sedgefield).
- 2245 hordwyrðne (MS hard wyrðne); 2247 mōstan (MS mæstan).
- 2250-2252 fȳra, þāra, [līf], secga seledrēam: heavily patched (MS fyrena, þana, no līf, gesawon). seledrēam taken in apposition to līf.
- 2253-2254 fe(o)r(mie), dug(uð), s[c]eōc (MS seoc).
- 2268 hwe(arf) vs MS hweop / Schücking wēop.
- 2275-2276 (swīðe ondrǣ)da(ð), (ho)r(d on) (Grein hearh on).
- 2283-2284 repeated hord (Bugge, Holthausen, Sedgefield, Cosijn variants noted).
- 2296 hlǣw (MS hlæwū); 2297 ealne ūtanweard (MS -weardne).
- 2297b-2299a: nē ðǣr ǣnig mon on þǣre wēstenne has no verb; Rieger/Sedgefield suspect a lacuna; Koeppel would strike 2296b-98a; wīges (MS hilde); bea(du)[we] weorces.
- 2305 se lāða (MS fela ða); 2307 læ[n]g (MS læg).

## Guesses in the English
- 2221 mid gewealdum ("of his own accord" from geweald "power"); synbysig (hapax-like) "sin-troubled".
- 2240 longgestrēona "long-treasures".
- 2243 nearocræftum fæst "fast with narrow-crafts" (cunning workmanship); nīwe "newly made".
- 2248 on ðē "from you" (alt. "in your keeping").
- 2249 frēcne adjective/adverb; 2252 Nāh with ic unstated.
- 2256 fǣtum "plates"; 2257 beadogrīma "battle-mask" (helmet vs visor).
- 2262 Næs (MS; Thorpe, Bugge and others nis); 2265 burhstede "stronghold-place".
- 2273 nacod "naked" (bare/unarmoured vs unsheathed).
- 2279 ēacencræftig "hugely powerful".
- 2283 rāsod "explored"; onboren "borne off".
- 2288 stonc (stincan "sniffed" vs "darted"); 2301 gefandod "tried / meddled with"; 2307 on wealle (which wall).
- 2292 unfǣge "not doomed"; the aside taken to be about the thief.

## New renderings proposed for the house table
wyrm = serpent (l) / dragon (i); ūhtsceaða = dawn-scather; ðēodsceaða = people-scather; hordwynn = hoard-joy; gryrebrōga = horror-terror; synbysig = sin-troubled; winegeōmor = friend-sad; longgestrēon = long-treasures; ēacencræftig = hugely powerful; seledrēam = hall-joy; feorhbealo = life-bale; gūðdēað = war-death; bealocwealm = baleful-death; glēobēam = glee-wood; beadogrīma = battle-mask; herepād = war-coat; hordærn = hoard-house; mandryhten = liege-lord; frioðowǣr = peace-pledge; sincgifa = treasure-giver (i: lord, giver of treasure); Waldend = Wielder (l) / Ruler (i), as in fitt-24.

## Other
- Abbreviation check: in the apparatus `Tho.` is Thorpe and `Thk.` is Thorkelin. The published fitt-31 note at 2208 expands `Tho.` as "Thorkelin"; the reviewer may want to check that (and any other fitt-31 notes using Tho.).
- Opening/closing quotation marks: the speech runs 2247-2266 and its quotes are carried in l/i.
